terms.gloss: woven cloth; in Traupman, a painter’s canvas
evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.4.1: negō ūllam pictūram in textilī (fuisse) (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Roman painters worked mostly on wood or walls (tabula, pariēs); the word itself is any woven fabric.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 168, 286.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
